title: Three-way SDK protocol normalization, stream helpers, and graceful reauth + compatibility bumps
author: Sofia Nguyen
release_notes: Normalize stream frame shapes across Python/TS/Go SDKs; add stream helper utilities; make auth token refresh non-blocking; bump SDK package versions to align protocol compatibility.
description: Summary: Implements protocol normalization for streaming payloads across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs, introduces small stream helper utilities (resume_point, safe_iterator), and makes the auth token refresh path non-blocking with graceful retry on 401. Includes compatibility bumps for all three SDK packages and a backport to the 1.x branch. Motivation: Multiple customers and internal integrations observed subtle framing differences between SDKs that caused stream-resume corner cases and double-reconnects under transient auth failures. This PR aligns wire shapes and improves ergonomics for consumers of streaming APIs while preserving backwards compatibility for normal usage. Checklist: [x] Add normalized stream frame encoder/decoder for all SDKs [x] Implement safe streaming helpers (resume_point, heartbeats) [x] Replace blocking token refresh with async refresh + queued retry [x] Add cross-sdk unit and integration tests [x] Update changelogs and bump versions [x] Backport small runtime fix to release/1.x High level commit summary: 1) python: add StreamFrame v2 codec, SafeStreamIterator, non-blocking token refresher; tests for resume semantics. 2) typescript: add FrameSerializer.normalize(), stream-utils.resumeFromCheckpoint(), tokenRefreshQueue; stream integration test against local echo server. 3) go: add framing package with NormalizeFrame, StreamCursor helper, token refresher that returns a retryable error type; update client interfaces to accept Option types for resume checkpoints. 4) docs: SDK changelogs and migration notes. Changed areas / illustrative files: - sdk/python/redwood_sdk/streaming/frame_v2.py (new codec) - sdk/python/redwood_sdk/streaming/helpers.py (SafeStreamIterator) - sdk/python/tests/test_stream_resume.py (integration) - sdk/ts/src/stream/frame-serializer.ts (normalize API) - sdk/ts/src/stream/stream-utils.ts (resume helpers) - sdk/ts/test/integration/stream-echo.test.ts - sdk/go/stream/framing/framing.go - sdk/go/client/stream_cursor.go - sdk/common/auth/token_refresher.go (shared logic) - build/ci/scripts/sdk-version-bump.sh Review conversation snapshot: Carlos: "Nice separation of concerns. Can we keep the old frame parser behind a feature flag for one release to ensure no downstream regressions?" Sofia: "Added a compatibility layer and a runtime toggle (REDWOOD_SDK_USE_LEGACY_FRAME) defaulting to false; documented in migration notes." Priya: "Token refresher change looks good but ensure that we cap concurrent refreshes per process." Sofia: "Added a singleflight-like gate in token_refresher with a max of 3 concurrent refreshes; updated unit tests." Ethan: "Small nit: rename resume_point to checkpoint for clarity." Sofia: "Renamed in all SDKs and left a deprecated alias for one release." CI summary: Initial runs flagged a flaky integration in TS stream tests (timeout on CI runner). Fixed by increasing the test harness timeout and adding a deterministic echo-mode in the test server. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, integration, lint, typecheck) after two reruns. QA notes: regression tests added for resume after token expiry and interleaved heartbeats. Backport: The framing bugfix was backported to release/1.x in a separate commit and tested against the on-prem runner used by customer SUP-1128. Release notes: Minor SDK changes; no breaking API changes for typical users. Consumers that implement custom binary framing will need to read migration notes. Merge: Squash merge into main (merge commit: author Sofia Nguyen), version bumps: python 0.7.4 -> 0.8.0, typescript 1.3.9 -> 1.4.0, go 0.9.1 -> 0.10.0. Follow-up: remove legacy frame flag after one release, monitor customer SDK telemetry for stream disconnects for two weeks.
